item.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
item.description:
The study shows how a malicious actor can edit fewer than ten dormant neurons in a large language model to turn it into a sleeper AI that executes a payload when a trigger is seen. It demonstrates this on models like Nemotron-Terminal-8B, Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT, achieving >98% success with no leakage on benign input, and notes a defense that flags over 90% of edited checkpoints.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud AI deployments, check all model weights for hidden neuron edits: 1) audit checkpoints for unexpected neuron activation patterns; 2) compare to a clean reference model; 3) implement runtime monitoring that flags sudden token‑generation spikes triggered by specific strings.

item.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
item.description:
The research shows a small open model can automatically learn policy rules from its own logs and improve performance by 12–19 points without a larger teacher. They built a system that diagnoses failures, writes rules, and fine‑tunes a LoRA adapter via reinforcement learning, achieving near‑frontier results. This is directly relevant to managing private LLM deployments.

IT Breakdown: If you manage private LLM deployments, here is what to do: 1. Deploy your model with on‑demand skills to capture policy in code. 2. Collect failure logs and run an automated rule‑generation pipeline that includes code checks, self‑review, retesting, and noise‑calibrated validation. 3. Fine‑tune a LoRA adapter with RL (GRPO) on the resulting multi‑turn, tool‑using conversations to improve reliability and policy adherence.

item.title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs
item.description:
LazyWeights improves memory usage for edge LLMs by compressing weight codes and decoding them on demand, reducing model size by up to 31% and cutting energy and latency by up to 38% on Jetson devices. It builds a Huffman‑encoded storage format and an ASIC decoder that fits in 0.21 mm², enabling faster, lower‑power inference on limited‑memory hardware. This directly impacts cloud infra managers who run or host edge models, offering a way to serve LLMs more efficiently on edge devices.

IT Breakdown: If you manage edge or low‑power inference workloads, adopt LazyWeights: 1) replace current quantisation with LazyWeights‑compatible GPTQ; 2) deploy the 0.21 mm² decoder ASIC or FPGA implementation; 3) monitor latency/energy reductions and adjust batch sizing accordingly.

item.title: [News] Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit has sparked government reactions across Asia, prompting supply‑chain confirmations and investigations into potential espionage and export‑control violations. The move threatens over $3 billion in AI projects that rely on Nvidia’s restricted processors, creating uncertainty for AI infrastructure globally.

item.title: [News] Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
item.description: The article highlights a surge in AI-fueled ransomware attacks, noting a 20‑40% increase in recent months and the use of large language models to craft more convincing phishing emails and streamline negotiations. It warns that while fully autonomous ransomware is not yet common, the trend suggests rapid evolution in threat tactics.

item.title: [News] Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Elon Musk, Replit, and Epic Games leaders joined a petition urging Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang after his resignation amid scandal. The move highlights leadership uncertainty that could ripple through AI funding and Nvidia's strategic direction.

item.title: [News] Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
item.description: Shield has upgraded its Forge platform with OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra, enabling AI agents to navigate legacy portals and automate routine support tasks that previously required human technicians. This improves response times for IT service providers handling ticketing, device, and license management systems lacking APIs.

item.title: [News] The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
item.description: A TechCrunch article highlights the growing number of AI projects and startups that have failed or shut down, citing examples such as Character.ai, Ollie, and several OpenAI initiatives. It notes that 42% of corporate AI ventures are abandoned, underscoring the volatility of the AI landscape.
